thread:
alex: noticed an ECC spike on us-west-2/gpu-pool-7 starting ~02:10 UTC, ~120 correctables/min on 4 cards. open to triage?
maya: saw alerts, auto-alerting hit but no uncorrectables yet. attaching quick metric: `ecc_rate: 118, 130, 95, 210` for the 4 noisy cards.
rohan: which kernel/driver on those hosts? recent roll?
alex: kernel `5.15.0-87`, nvidia-driver `530.41`. we rolled those last week during the maintenance window.
sylvia: correlated with a batch job spike? any hot loops?
alex: not according to job history, throughput steady. EOS: suspicious pattern of bursty correctables after long idle intervals.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1942356789. tagging @oncall.
jonas: could be thermal or power; telemetry from those hosts looks fine (temps 67-72C). logs show repeated `GPU_ECC_CORRECTABLE` entries.
maya: proposal: introduce a soft-drain that triggers at sustained correctable rate >100/min for 3 consecutive 1-min windows, but only if correctable:uncorrectable ratio > 100:1. avoids noisy but harmless bursts. thoughts?
rohan: prefer adding a cooldown and rate-limiter so we don't thrash scheduling. e.g. a card enters soft-drain for 30m and we cap re-drain attempts to 1 per 12h.
sylvia: also add KV cache eviction for in-flight contexts to reduce replays when draining.
alex: proposed action items in order: 1) add metric alert to annotate cards with `noisy_ecc=true` 2) apply soft-drain policy 3) create canary with 3 nodes in us-east-1 to validate policy 4) schedule replacement if hardware continues noisy for 24h.
jonas: runbook question: should soft-drain be cluster-scoped or instance-scoped? if cluster, we risk capacity shortage for single-customer clusters.
maya: instance-scoped. only mark the GPU as unschedulable on that host and migrate pods where feasible. keep reserved capacity fallback for Dedicated customers.
rohan: edge case: Xid errors and occasional uncorrectables — if we see a single uncorrectable (Xid 31/43) escalate immediately to force-evac and hw-replace. define threshold: any uncorrectable => immediate replace. agreed?
sylvia: +1. uncorrectables are not safe to ignore. also collect full nvsmi/gpu logs before replacement with `nvidia-smi --query --format=csv` and dmesg snippet.
alex: drafting automation: `if correctable_rate >= 100/min for 3m -> mark soft-drain; if corrective persists and correctable_rate >= 200/min for 30m -> schedule hw-replace ticket; if uncorrectable_count >=1 -> immediate hw-evac + replace`
maya: can we add a temporary traffic-shed policy instead of immediate full drain? graceful migrating low-priority jobs first, keep high-priority Dedicated workloads pinned with fallback to other pools.
rohan: implement priority-aware eviction: evict preemptible/batch first, then attempt live-migration for Dedicated. that reduces customer impact.
ci-bot: ci pipeline job `infra/auto-drain` created: PR #3427 with tests for threshold gating.
jonas: experiment suggestion: replay recent traffic on canary nodes with synthetic ECC generator to validate false-positive rate <1%.
sylvia: note: hardware vendors warn that some driver versions correlate with higher correctable reporting; add driver-version histogram to monitoring so we can group by driver and firmware.
alex: ops cost note: if we replace hardware too aggressively we'll burn spares. propose we maintain a 24h persistent-noise window before replacing unless uncorrectable seen.
maya: summary proposal (for approval): 1) soft-drain rule: sustained >=100/min for 3m -> soft-drain 30m cooldown; 2) escalator: >=200/min for 30m -> create hw-replace ticket; 3) immediate replace on any uncorrectable; 4) priority-aware eviction; 5) canary validation + driver-version tagging.
rohan: +1 from infra. I'll review PR and add rate-limiter changes.
sylvia: +1 from runtime. I'll add KV eviction step and logging.
jonas: +1 from ops. schedule spare allocation check.
alex: ok, I'll ship the PR to canary tomorrow morning and open a deployment window. timeline: canary 2h test, if green roll to us-west-2 primary pool with 1h observation.
maya: adding a follow-up task: postmortem if more than 5 replaced cards in 7d so we can do vendor RMA audit.
ops-bot: note: scheduled task `infra/hw-replace` created for ticketing automation.
alex: thanks all — moving to implement. will ping #incidents for any escalations. :thumbsup:
